about: The makers of art this kit knows, as rows of data. A new maker costs a row and at most one small adapter file in builder/art/adapters/. Read by builder/art/providers.mjs; checked by tests/art.test.mjs. `tier` places a row in the order of choice (see `order`). `reach.via` says how it is reached: `files` (the person hands over a file), `env` (the person's own key in an environment variable, read at the moment of the call and never written anywhere by us), `mcp` (a connection the person added to their own agent: their session calls it and hands us the file), `session` (the person's own running session makes it: our tool hands over a request and takes back SVG, a pixel grid or a file; our code makes no model call), `library` (the asset library: library/packs and your private packs), `kit` (the kit's own stand-ins). Prices, licences and limits are quoted from each service's own pages on the `checked` date and will go stale: `docs/ART.md` says to re-read them. `run` says what was really run against the service when the row was written. Nothing here signs anyone in, stores a token, or sends a request to a model on a person's subscription.

kinds.picture: one picture of one thing (a prop, a marker, an icon)
kinds.sheet: a body sheet: a character's frames in one picture (builder/art/standard.mjs)
kinds.tile: a ground or wall tile that repeats

prefer.about: When a person has offered several connections for the same kind, the one they name wins: GF_ART_PICTURE, GF_ART_SHEET, GF_ART_TILE or GF_ART_MODEL in the environment (a row id; `session` or `stand-in` to skip connections), else the first row below.

licence.note: yours to state: record where the file came from and its licence in the game's ATTRIBUTION.md

providers.name: OpenAI Images API

cost.note: billed by tokens to the key's account. OpenAI's own per-picture figures for gpt-image-2 at 1024x1024: low $0.006, medium $0.053, high $0.211; per-picture figures for the gpt-image-2.5 models are in an interactive calculator only

licence.note: "Customer: (a) retains all ownership rights in Input; and (b) owns all Output." (OpenAI Services Agreement, section 4.1)

estimate.note: about one cent a picture at low quality (an estimate; the real cost is on your OpenAI usage page)

providers.limits: A body sheet is not offered: one prompt does not give six frames of one character on a grid.
providers.run: fixtures (no OPENAI_API_KEY on the machine this was built on)

providers.name: Meshy

cost.note: prepaid credits; creating a key "requires a paid plan". Text to 3D: preview 20 credits + refine 10; image to 3D with textures 30; rigging 5; an animation 3. The kit's own tools use about 36 credits for a prop and 41 for a rigged body

licence.note: "If you are on a premium plan, you own all assets you create with Meshy." "If you are on a free plan, we grant you a CC BY 4.0 license instead."

estimate.note: about 36 credits a prop, 41 a rigged body (the kit's ledger counts the real figure)

providers.run: not run this time (no key on the machine this was built on); the tools behind it are the kit's existing `gamesfun meshy`, used for real in games.fun

providers.name: Tripo

can.rig: a separate task: biped, quadruped and five more

cost.note: credits per task; the documentation does not state how many per task or what a credit costs ("Different task types consume different numbers of credits."; "Failed and cancelled tasks are not charged."). Each finished task reports `credits_consumed`, which we record

licence.note: NOT ESTABLISHED: Tripo's terms and pricing pages refused our fetch on 2026-10-11. Read https://www.tripo3d.ai/terms yourself before shipping a Tripo model

estimate.note: unknown until a task finishes; check your balance in the Tripo console first

providers.run: fixtures (no Tripo key on the machine this was built on; the environment variable's name is ours, Tripo's docs name none)
